chunks: On the day He will gather them together, (He will say:) 'O you assembly of jinns, you made great use of men.' But their proteges among men will say: 'O our Lord, we lived a life of mutual gain, but have now reached the term You ordained for us.' 'Your abode is Hell,' He will say, 'where you will dwell for ever, unless God please otherwise.' Verily your Lord is wise and all-knowing.

key_terms.اسْتَكْثَرْتُمْ: You made great use of / multiplied

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between jinns and humans on the Day of Judgment according to this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the mutual entrapment of humans and jinns, where humans often viewed jinns as allies or patrons, leading to a shared fate in Hell. The phrase 'except for what He wills' (إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ) is interpreted by scholars like Al-Tabarsi as indicating that Allah may grant mercy to some based on His wisdom, even within the general decree of punishment, underscoring the balance between divine justice and mercy.
